<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via packages.enable (sdk, the route ledger binds it to PATCH /packages/:id/enable))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via /packages/:id/enable (route, a path literal in REFUSAL_SENTENCE; a path literal in a comment in PositionSchema; a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`  _(via /packages/:id/enable (route, a path literal in REFUSAL_SENTENCE; a path literal in a comment in PositionSchema; a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx`  _(via /packages/:id/enable (route, a path literal in REFUSAL_SENTENCE; a path literal in a comment in PositionSchema; a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via PositionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via PositionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via PositionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via /packages/:id/enable (route, a path literal in REFUSAL_SENTENCE; a path literal in a comment in PositionSchema; a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b888a41efdbd00853bf8cc919cf694747c59372b` — the merge of head `c60334587961089261f6a49f1e3dcc6f9fa71433` into base `8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b888a41efdbd00853bf8cc919cf694747c59372b && git checkout b888a41efdbd00853bf8cc919cf694747c59372b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2 c60334587961089261f6a49f1e3dcc6f9fa71433 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2 && git merge --no-ff c60334587961089261f6a49f1e3dcc6f9fa71433

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `27a39b8799dcbfc0e4e22198811fc46f7ffb9b3f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts

PR #33642 (`Refs #33301`), net diff against `main` at merge base `4c32b969`: 7 files. Cited code read on `main` at `020ce3d9`, and `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` again at `babd5d4a` (live `main`, after #33527).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged, right.** `renamedFrom` stays `z.array(SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema).optional()`. No key, value, default or refinement moves.
- **Public surface: one description string, right.** The `.describe()` text of `PositionSchema.renamedFrom` changes, and with it the generated row in `content/docs/references/identity/position.mdx`. The row is the describe text word for word, and no other copy of the old sentence is left in the tree at this head.
- **Runtime bytes: one log string, right.** `REFUSAL_SENTENCE['claimant-disabled']` in `position-renamed-holder-carry.ts` is the only shipped change in `@objectstack/plugin-security`. The refusal reason `claimant-disabled`, its conditions and its order are untouched, and no test pins the sentence.
- **No behaviour change.** Everything else is jsdoc and module-doc text.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec: patch` (`33301-renamed-from-install-enable-announce.md`): right. A description changes; nothing an author can write changes.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch` (`33301-claimant-disabled-log-reason.md`): right. A warning's wording ships in `dist`; a patch is the level for it.
- Both new changesets carry `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on lines of their own, and both are right.
- **The two foreign edits are true corrections under ruling D of #17712.** Both notes are pending on `main`, and the code falsifies the sentences replaced:
  - `.changeset/33301-renamed-from-carry-text.md`: "a package install or enable that does not announce" is false since #33448 (`announcePackageReload`, both doors); "a hot upgrade over a version the kernel still serves ... carried at the next restart" is false since #33050 (`SchemaRegistry.replacingPackageBody`), pinned on a real kernel by #33473. The replacement sentence agrees with the code.
  - `.changeset/33238-position-rename-hot-install.md`: the removed bullet ("install and enable routes, which do not announce") is false for the same reason. The added bullet names the right doors, the right spelling (`app/ID`), the right package and card (`@objectstack/runtime`, #33302), and the disabled case.
  This record confirms the `check-empty-changeset` refusal of those two files as the declared DELIBERATE CORRECTION.
- **should-fix (PR body, no push): `Check Changeset` is red for a second reason that is not declared.** The run on this head fails two steps. The first is the foreign-changeset refusal above. The second is `check-changeset-no-major`: "LEVEL AXIS: NOT MEASURED ... the `Metadata-protocol:` line was not readable", reason `inline-key`, because the PR body spells the pair on one bulleted line (`- Clause-②: no. Metadata-protocol: none.`, under "Acceptance notes"). The level gate therefore gave no verdict on this head, and the declared red hides it. Remedy: give `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` each a line of its own in the PR body; the gate re-reads the body on the `edited` event. After that the check should be red for the two foreign files only. This record does not cover the level-axis refusal.
- nit (changeset prose): with PR 1's pending note corrected in place, the new spec note describes a correction to text no release ever shipped ("The description listed ... among the cases carried at the next restart"). The two spec notes will publish side by side. Harmless to the level.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the round 1 or round 2 reports of this PR (6888832695, 6889125131). The earlier question in 6887039708 (who opens this follow-up) is answered by claim 6888561756.
- Deviations, each judged:
  - Hand re-application of the prepared patch after #33473 rewrote the module doc: accepted, the result is read below.
  - Dropping "a hot upgrade over a still-served version ... carried at the next restart": right, the code and #33473's test falsify it.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-security` changeset added in round 2 for the warning string: right.
  - Surface breach against claim 6888561756 ("header comment only", no foreign changesets): the warning string and the two pending notes were added at the seat's request in round 2. Named here so the seat's ACCEPT owns it.
- **Escalate: the ADR-0150 addendum on `main` is now false, and its carrier is closed.** #33568 merged at 2026-11-15T04:13Z and closed #33301. Line 288 of the ADR on live `main` still says "a hot upgrade over a version the running kernel still serves ... carried at the next restart". The dev routed this to "the card's ADR follow-up", but the card is closed and this PR is `Refs`. It needs a new Tier H card.
- Out of this PR's scope, noted: since #33527 (live `main`) the disable door announces `app/ID` too. A package that renamed a position and is then disabled will log the `claimant-disabled` warning at that disable, also when no holder is left on the old name. The texts in this PR stay true under it.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts`** (jsdoc and `.describe()` of `renamedFrom`), each changed sentence against the code:

- "a hot install-local install or upgrade (the re-register withdraws the position the new version no longer ships ...)": holds. `registerApp` runs every package body through `replacingPackageBody` (`packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts`, `registry.ts`), which withdraws the item slots the previous body wrote and the new one did not. install-local then announces `changed: ['app/ID']`. #33473's test in `marketplace-install-local-hot-resync.test.ts` drives v1 then v2 through the real door on a real kernel with the real `SecurityPlugin`, and its ablation went red on the withdrawal line.
- "the runtime `POST /packages` install": holds. `announcePackageReload(deps, _context, pkgId, 'installed')` runs after the registry write and before the lifecycle-refusal return, so on both answers.
- "a `PATCH /packages/:id/enable` that switches a disabled package on": holds. `if (wasDisabled) await announcePackageReload(..., 'enabled')`, after `registry.enablePackage(id)`. An enable of an enabled package announces nothing, which the wording excludes. `packages-reload-announce.test.ts` moves a holder through this door on a real composition.
- "A package still disabled when its announcement is heard is refused (`claimant-disabled`) until the enable that switches it on announces it again": holds. `positionRenameReloadScope` admits `app/ID` whenever `registry.getPackage(ID)` is non-null, disabled or not; `carryRenamedPositionHolders` adds the disabled packages' positions to the claims and refuses a disabled claimant.
- "An artifact reload that names only its file is carried at the next restart": holds, unchanged in substance. The file watcher's `_reloadAndAnnounce` sends a path, which `positionRenameReloadScope` does not admit.
- The describe sentence ("an install or hot upgrade, the enable of a disabled package, a per-item publish, a publish of drafts ... A package still disabled then is carried when it is enabled") agrees with the jsdoc and the code.

Findings:

- **nit.** The jsdoc lists "the runtime `POST /packages` install" beside the other doors without saying what it can carry. `ManifestSchema` declares no `positions` key, so an install body ships no position; the door carries only renames the package already holds (a publish registered them). Its one case with an effect is the overwrite install with `enableOnInstall: true` of a disabled package, which is the case #33448's test pins. The sentence is true of the announcement; the `.describe()` text does not name the door and is unaffected.
- **nit.** "until the enable that switches it on announces it again" names one of two doors: an overwrite install with `enableOnInstall: true` also switches the package on and announces it.
- **nit.** The re-wrapped jsdoc leaves one short line ("system, in every organization, it moves each").

**`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts`** (module doc "When it runs", and the warning string):

- "The runtime's package install (`POST /packages`) and the enable of a disabled package (`PATCH /packages/:id/enable`) announce `app/ID` too, so they are carried at once; an install that leaves the package disabled is refused `claimant-disabled` until that enable announces it": holds, as above.
- "A package the announcement does not name is carried at the next boot": holds; a reload run judges only claims in its scope.
- Warning string, "enabling it through `PATCH /packages/:id/enable` carries them, and so does the first boot after it is enabled": holds. The enable door announces a package that was disabled, the reload run judges it with the package enabled, and the boot run judges every claim. Like the old sentence, it assumes no other refusal stands at that run.

Findings:

- **nit.** The same file's refusal list was not updated: lines 48 to 51 still say of `claimant-disabled` "the next boot after the package is enabled carries". After this PR the module doc says two things about one refusal. A comment only; it ships nothing.

Tried to break it: an upgrade after a restart (the boot rehydrate registers through the same `registerApp`, so the previous body is recorded and the withdrawal runs); an install that lands disabled (refused, then carried by the enable); an enable of an enabled package (no announce, excluded by the wording); a failed announce (logged at `warn` with the restart that repairs it, the door still answers); #33527's disable and uninstall announcements (nothing carried). None falsifies a sentence in the two files.

No must-fix. One should-fix, in ②, on the PR body. Nits may be left or folded on the prose faces.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-2qw5ej`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5mswnWm181XgYcCUag`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `85543852746186b7a2439f6aa0e5db6e4a09a104`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts

Delta review of record 6889204599 (PASS at `27a39b87`). PR #33642 (`Refs #33301`), net diff against `main` at merge base `3c0033f9`: the same 7 files. Cited code read on `main` at `3c0033f9`, and `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` again at `8f915f2a` (live `main`, after #33622).

What moved since `27a39b87`: two merges of `main` (`a65f04fa`, `85543852`) and two commits, `a797bffe` and `e3ff5da1`. The net diff at this head, set against the net diff reviewed at `27a39b87`, differs in exactly the hunks of those two commits: the `claimant-disabled` bullet of the carry's module doc, the install-local qualification in the carry's "When it runs", the `renamedFrom` jsdoc and `.describe()`, the regenerated `position.mdx` row, and one sentence of `.changeset/33301-renamed-from-install-enable-announce.md`. The merges added nothing to the net diff. The two foreign changesets, the `claimant-disabled` changeset and the warning string are byte-identical to the reviewed head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged, right.** `renamedFrom` stays `z.array(SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema).optional()`. The delta moves no key, value, default or refinement.
- **Public surface: the same one description string, right.** The delta rewords the `.describe()` text of `PositionSchema.renamedFrom` once more. The `position.mdx` row is that text word for word, and no other copy of either the old or the round-2 sentence is left in a generated file at this head.
- **Runtime bytes: none new.** `a797bffe` and the carry hunk of `e3ff5da1` are module-doc comments. The one shipped string, `REFUSAL_SENTENCE['claimant-disabled']`, is as reviewed.
- **No behaviour change.**

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec: patch` and `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`: right, as in 6889204599. The delta adds one sentence to the spec note and changes no level.
- Both new changesets carry `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on lines of their own. The PR body now does too, and the level gate reads them: `check-changeset-no-major` on this head answers "LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② `no` and metadata-protocol `none` ... a non-protocol change at `patch`". The should-fix of 6889204599 is closed.
- **The two foreign edits are still true corrections**, re-read against `main` at `3c0033f9`:
  - `.changeset/33238-position-rename-hot-install.md`: install-local is scoped as "for the positions of the package it names (`app/ID`)", which already agrees with the new qualification. The runtime install announces on both answers (`packages.ts` ~:2808), the enable only when the package was disabled (~:2883), and a disabled claimant is refused. "An uninstall's announcement names a package no longer registered" holds; #33546's disable announcement names a package still held and disabled, which is refused `claimant-disabled`, so it carries nothing either.
  - `.changeset/33301-renamed-from-carry-text.md`: holds. Its list is conditioned on "announces the position or its package as registered", so a package the door does not announce is outside the sentence.
- `Check Changeset` on this head (run 132706980166) fails one step, `check-empty-changeset`, with two errors, one per foreign file. Every other step is green. This record confirms that refusal as the declared DELIBERATE CORRECTION.
- nit (changeset prose): `33301-renamed-from-carry-text.md` still paraphrases the description as "(an install or hot upgrade, ...)", while the describe text it announces now reads "an install or hot upgrade of the package the door announces" and names the other packages of a multi-package artifact. Not false, and the PR's own spec note carries the qualification. The two notes publish side by side.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none. The card carries no round-3 dev report for this branch; the newest for it is 6889125131 (round 2), whose list is empty. The round-3 account is in the PR body only. The two newer reports on the card (6889297872, 6889459761) are #33653's, both with empty lists.
- The escalation of 6889204599 (ADR-0150 line 288) is answered: the seat reopened the card (6889216860) and #33653 carries the ADR wording. Its install-local clause and this PR's say the same thing.
- **should-fix (PR body, no push): `PR-body guards` is red on this head, and it is not the declared red.** The newest run (132706965170, 05:05Z) fails `check:closing-target-claim`: "PR #33642 closes #33656 with no `Claim:` on the card naming `claude/project-thread-2qw5ej`". The body's "What changes" bullet says "code fix #33656", and `fix #33656` is a closing keyword. The run before that body edit (05:03Z) was green. As written, merging this text-only PR would close #33656, the open card for the install-local code fix. Remedy: reword the reference so that no closing keyword precedes the number (for example "the code change is tracked in #33656"); the guard re-reads the body on the `edited` event. Do not land while this check is red. This record does not cover the refusal.
- Follow-up owed by #33656, named so it is not lost: when install-local announces every package of a multi-package artifact, the sentences this delta adds become false in five places (the `renamedFrom` jsdoc and describe, the `position.mdx` row, the carry's "When it runs", and the spec note if still pending). That change has to carry them.
- Out of scope, as before: since #33527/#33546 the disable door announces `app/ID`, so a disable of a package that renamed a position logs the `claimant-disabled` warning. The texts stay true under it.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts`**, each sentence the delta changed:

- "a hot install-local install or upgrade, for the package the door announces": holds. `announceHotInstall` triggers `metadata:reloaded` with `changed: ['app/<manifestId>']` and nothing else (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` :6805 at `3c0033f9`, :6849 on live `main`). `manifestId` is the artifact's own `manifest.id`.
- "The other packages of a multi-package artifact, which install-local does not announce, ... are carried at the next restart": holds. The `manifest` service's `register` (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` ~:1045) calls `registerApp` once per `packages[]` entry, each under its own id, so the registry holds every member. `positionRenameReloadScope` admits only the `app/ID` entries of the payload, and `carryRenamedPositionHolders` keeps a claim only when its position's package is in that scope, so a member the door did not name is not judged at that reload. The boot run judges every claim.
- "and an artifact reload that names only its file": unchanged in substance, holds.
- The `.describe()` sentence ("an install or hot upgrade of the package the door announces ... The other packages of a multi-package artifact, and an artifact reload that names only its file, are carried at the next restart") agrees with the jsdoc and the code. The runtime `POST /packages` door takes one manifest and announces its id, so the phrase fits that door as well.

Findings:

- **nit.** "the package the door announces" presumes the announced id is a package. On a multi-package artifact the wrapper's id "names no package unless one of them carries it" (the door's own comment, ~:2569), and the residual gets no package record. In that case `app/<manifestId>` is no scope, nothing is carried at once, and every member waits for the restart. The sentences stay true ("the other packages" is then all of them); the carry header's "(the door names only the artifact's own id)" says it more exactly than the jsdoc.
- **nit.** The re-wrapped jsdoc has one line of about 110 columns ("no longer reads as declared), the runtime `POST /packages` install, a `PATCH ...` that") and two short ones ("the next restart. As the" / "system, in every organization, it moves each").
- The three nits of 6889204599 on this file stand as accepted deviations; the delta does not touch them.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts`**:

- `claimant-disabled` bullet (:48-51), "enabling it through `PATCH /packages/:id/enable` carries, and so does the next boot after it is enabled": holds. The enable door announces a package that was disabled (`if (wasDisabled) await announcePackageReload(..., 'enabled')`, after `registry.enablePackage`), the reload run then judges the claim with the package served, and the boot run judges every claim. It now agrees with `REFUSAL_SENTENCE['claimant-disabled']` at :693. This closes the nit of 6889204599.
- "A hot install-local install or upgrade is carried at once for the package the door announces; the other packages of a multi-package artifact are carried at the next restart (the door names only the artifact's own id)": holds, as above.
- The rest of "When it runs" is as reviewed, and still agrees with `packages.ts` on `main` after #33546: install on both answers, enable only from disabled, a disable announced and refused.

No finding on this file.

Tried to break the delta: a member of a multi-package artifact reached by another announcement (a per-item publish or publish-drafts names `position/NAME` and carries it sooner; "at the next restart" is the latest, as for the artifact reload); an install-local upgrade of a multi-package artifact (each member's re-register withdraws its dropped position, but only the announced id is judged); the lenient install path (nothing registered, no announce, the restart's rehydrate and boot run carry); the disable announcement (held and disabled, refused); live `main` after #33622 (the announce is unchanged). None falsifies a sentence.

No must-fix. One should-fix, in ③, on the PR body. Nits may be left or folded on the prose faces.

Check-runs on `85543852`: 76 runs, all completed. 57 success, 14 skipped, 1 cancelled (a superseded `Check Changeset`), 4 failure: `Check Changeset` twice (the declared two foreign notes) and `PR-body guards` twice (the closing keyword above). Build, lint, type-check, Test Core 1-8 and Test UI 1-16 are green.

Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5mswnWm181XgYcCUag`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## ACCEPT · PR #33642 (#33301 follow-up, Refs) · head `c60334587961089261f6a49f1e3dcc6f9fa71433` · 2026-11-15T06:05Z

## 席位核对
